raw_analysis_notes: 0x2A confirmed as checksum algorithm selector: 0=None(3.4), 2=CRC64(default 3.14), 4=SHA256. Immutable on upgrade: Win10-formatted volumes always 0=None even after 3.14 upgrade. Volume flags at 0x2C: Win10=0x06 (bits 0x02+0x04) vs Win11=0x66 (bits 0x02+0x04+0x20+0x40). Bit 0x02=mount marker (set by driver on first mount, RefsMountVolume decompiled). Bit 0x40=gates VBR 0x2A checksum algo (insider: 'used only if flags bit 6 set'). 0x30-0x37 always zero (reserved). See report_boot_sector_deep_analysis.md | RE-VERIFIED 2026-06-18 (all-disk): claimed flags are 0x06(Win10)/0x66(Win11); disk shows 0x26 is the genuine v3.7/v3.9 value (already documented in structure_reference Subtable A.1c), so the two-value summary in FS_VBR_012 is wrong/incomplete.

description: $DATA: the file's content stream. Whether its bytes are INLINE in the record or in on-disk EXTENTS is a property of the VOLUME FORMAT, not of the attribute: on format <=3.10 main $DATA is never inline (Prade et al.'s 'always non-resident' is correct, scoped to those formats); from format 3.11 it is inline while the stream is under 0x800 (2048 B). The 0x20000 (128 KiB) figure is the NAMED-STREAM cap, not a main-data threshold (see MD_ADS_RA_003), and named streams are NOT 'always resident' - 729 of 8,238 are extent-backed. Residency must be read from the $DATA descriptor's own form, never from the name row's length or its key_flags (E77/E87).
static_analysis_notes: Type code 0x80 confirmed in RefsCheckValidAttributeAccess. The residency gate is RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite (win11 26100 @1400ddd2c): format <0x30b (3.11) or size <0x800 stays inline, else RefsConvertToNonResident. RefsCheckValidResidentDataAttribute - the DATA-specific validity check - exists only in the v3.14-era drivers; win10 17134 has only the generic RefsCheckValidResidentAttribute and no RefsConvertToNonResident at all. Merged from MD_RESD_SA_001.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-04, corpus manifest r2 (79 distinct volumes / 507,433 file name rows). Format <=3.10: 5,419 rows over 14 volumes, INLINE=0 and EMPTY=0 - every main $DATA extent-backed, the smallest a 5-byte file holding a whole 4 KiB cluster. Format >=3.11: largest inline 2,047 B, 0 of 399,225 inline rows reach 2,048. PREVIOUS RD CELL WITHDRAWN: 'Win10: 100% resident for small test files. Win11: ~92% resident. Threshold confirmed empirically.' was produced by the value-length>84 rule, which measures RECORD PLACEMENT, not residency - it is the circular reading E87 corrects, and it is contradicted by the descriptor-level measurement above.

Records are laid out 8-BYTE ALIGNED, so the step to the next record is roundup8(record_size). Measured over 48,474 records / 40 images (0 violations) and 30,524 consecutive row pairs (99.6% gap == roundup8(record_size); the rest are unused node space).

description: Object Table row value header decoded: 8xu32 (format=2, reserved, key_off=0x18, val_off=0x30, payload_offset@u32[4], payload_length@u32[5], generation, dirty_gen) + LCN tuple (4xQ) + checksum. Generation counter at u32[6] = checkpoint virtual clock. All-disk verified 2026-07-06: 34603 OT rows across 114 ReFS images, 0 violations; off@0x10 flat within each family; compact size tracks checksum size (80/88 default, 104/112 SHA-256), independent of cluster size.

description: Complete embedded attribute taxonomy with dual-marker system. The genuine embedded-attribute type-code set is EXACTLY 10 codes: 0x38/0x39 ($OBJ_LINK), 0x80 ($DATA), 0x90 ($I30_INDEX), 0xB0 ($SNAPSHOT/ADS), 0xC0 ($REPARSE), 0xD0 ($EA_INFO), 0xE0 ($EA), 0xF0 (USN $Max), 0x100 ($EFS); 0x50/0x60/0xA0 NEVER appear as embedded sub-records. Marker 0x80000001: single-instance (0x80 DATA header/0xC0 REPARSE/0xD0 EA_INFO/0xE0 EA / 0xF0 USN $Max). Marker 0x80000002: multi-instance (0x39 FileRef/0x80 DATA stream/0xB0 Named Stream/0x100 $EFS). 0xB0 format: val[0x04]=0x68=EXTENDED/non-inline (snapshots OR a large >=2KB ADS) vs !=0x68=INLINE (small ADS); val[0x10] is the ADS(0)-vs-snapshot(2) discriminator (E61). 532503 entries (526454 with markers + 6049 unclassified) across 409185 files on 112 images. LOWER BOUND (E73): this census was taken with an outer-level-only embedded parse, which missed attributes held in a child node (4094 further records over 19 images); the counts here are minima, not totals.

description: ReFS file deletion flow: RefsDeleteFile → MsDeleteRow (removes from directory B+ tree) → MsReparentFileToTrash → CmsTrashTable::AddFileTable (OID 0xD queues for cleanup) → background TrashCleanerWorkItemMethod → DeleteFileTable (frees data extents). CoW ensures old directory pages persist. Recovery: (1) Trash Table scan (2) checkpoint comparison (3) orphaned MSB+ page scan. Updated by E64: recovery is two-mode (recovery/--full) and IDENTITY-based (name+create_time); embedded-record files bypass the Trash via RefsDeleteResidentDataScbAndCommit so only split-record files + directories are reparented; live-page + orphan-page B+-tree node slack (FS_DEL_RA_005) is the primary method.

description: Reparse Index (OID 0x540/0x541 schema 0x160) key structure decoded (24 bytes): u32 marker 0x80000001 @0 (single-instance embedded-subrecord marker; the "key_type=0x0001/key_flags=0x8000" split is just a coincidental LE re-read of this u32) + ReparseTag(u32)@4 + _REFS_FILE_REFERENCE(16B)@8. The 16B file-ref is the file's 128-bit reference: word0 (entry ordinal/file-key, small 2..32) @8, containing-directory OID @0x10 (both from [fcb+0x58]+0xf8/+0x100). DISK-VERIFIED 2026-07-05: every index OID@0x10 matches a reparse file's PARENT directory OID (242/242 across 3 images: mftecmd 93/93, insider 42/42, specials 107/107) -- it is the containing directory's OID, NOT a per-file 'own' OID (ReFS files have none). Value: minimal/empty (pure existence index). ONE row per reparse-bearing OBJECT (FCB), inserted by RefsCreateReparsePointInternal via MsInsertRow(...,0x32), deleted by RefsDeleteReparsePointInternal/RefsRemoveReparsePoint via MsDeleteRow. NO tag filter -- ALL tags indexed (mount/symlink/WSL/etc); enumerate uses a match-ALL cursor.

description: Integrity stream extents use variable-stride entries. Checksum page entries (flags=0x1c00d0): 32 bytes (24-byte entry + 8-byte CRC suffix) always run_len=1. Data run entries (flags=0x180040): standard 24 bytes variable run_len. Both types point to real file data. Table header format identical to normal extents. CORRECTION (E86): flags=0x1c00d0 is not a distinct entry kind - it is (record_size 0x1c = 28) | (flags 0xd0), i.e. the run_length==1 instance of the checksummed family. The family is flags 0xd0 with record_size 24 + run*4; runs from 11 to 223 are observed on the corpus (e.g. record_size 916 with run 223). The '8-byte CRC suffix' is a 4-byte CRC32-C plus 4 bytes of 8-byte-alignment padding, which is why the step for the run==1 case is 32 (roundup8(28)). A fixed-stride walk that advances 24 unless the u32 equals 0x1c00d0 therefore MISPARSES any checksummed record with run>1; that is why such files failed their coverage check and reported an undecodable holder until E86.

description: key_flags is u16 at key+0x02, NOT the first 4 bytes of the row header. Values 0x68/0x2a8 are row sizes. key_flags take ONLY {0x01, 0x02}; 0x04 NEVER appears. The flag encodes RECORD PLACEMENT, not data residency (E77): 0x01 = the name row EMBEDS the object's record; 0x02 = the name row is an INDEX ENTRY whose record was split into a type-0x40 backing in the home directory. Neither value says where the file's data lives - residency must be read from the $DATA attribute's storage. (Measured: every kf=0x01 FILE row is extent-backed on v3.4/3.7/3.9/3.10 - 1120/250/386/236 rows, zero inline; on v3.14 219,960 of 236,769 are inline.) Directories are key_flags 0x02 with the directory attribute bit 0x10000000 set in the value attribute word (value+0x40), NOT a separate 0x04 flag. Distribution 111 images/525K entries: {0x01: 409483 ; 0x02: 115682 ; 0x04: 0}. Errata E15/E17 "0x04=directory" was wrong.

It is the driver's own link list, so it is the authoritative answer to 'what are this object's names' and the basis for hard-link grouping. Two caveats when counting: some backings carry the SAME pair twice, byte-for-byte (deduplicate), and the rows exist only on objects with their own record - 0 of 219 embedded (key_flags 0x01) file rows carry one, and on v3.4 no directory does (0/309). Enables path reconstruction from the Object Table alone. Driver: RefsInitializeObjLinkRow.

description: CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (E87/MD_ADS_RA_003). The earlier headline - 'ALL alternate data streams are inline (159/159); the genuine non-resident ADS claim is REFUTED' - was measured on 159 rows, none of which reached 2 KiB, and it already contradicted E61 in this register. Corrected: of 8,238 true named streams (8,353 0xB0 rows less 115 snapshot-name entries), 7,505 are inline, 4 empty and 729 EXTENT-BACKED. On format >=3.11 no named stream of 2,048 B or more is inline and the extent-backed ones begin at exactly 2,048 - the driver's 0x800, the same constant it applies to main $DATA. The attribute-flags bit 0x1000 at val+0x02 DOES separate them: set on exactly the 844 non-inline rows (729 extent-backed + 115 snapshot entries), clear on exactly the 7,509 inline/empty ones, 0 violations. What survives from the original row is the ADS/snapshot discriminator: StreamSummary flags (u16) at val+0x10, 0 = ADS and 2 = snapshot (MD_SNAP_RA_005) - independently re-confirmed here, since every val+0x10 == 2 row names an existing $DATA sub-id > 0x1000 on its host, 115 of 115.

E20 (ADS always inline) HOLDS for ADS <2KB; a >=2KB ADS is extent-backed via a type-0x0 record (E61 - byte-exact on a 256B-2MB sweep). | CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (E87/MD_ADS_RA_003): named streams are NOT always inline. Census of every 0xB0 row - 8,353 rows / 57 images, 0 unrecognised - gives 7,505 inline, 4 empty, 729 EXTENT-backed and 115 snapshot-name entries. The earlier 'always resident' rests on samples that were all small: on format >=3.11 a named stream of 2,048 B or more is never inline, and 13 smaller ones are extent-backed too because their writer pre-allocated (alloc != size, the E60 rule).

description: Hard-link mechanism (v3.14): each name = a separate type-0x30 INDEX-ENTRY dir entry (key_flags 0x02, 84B value). E77: 'index entry' not 'split-record file' - key_flags encodes RECORD PLACEMENT (0x01 the row embeds the file's record; 0x02 the record was split into a type-0x40 backing), NOT data residency; a kf=0x02 FILE row is the fingerprint of a move or hard link (51/51 measured) and the form does not exist on v3.4 (0 type-0x40 rows, 0 kf=0x02 file rows). value+0x00 = per-directory child ordinal (= NextFileId $SI+0x58), shared by one file's names but NOT a globally-unique FileId (reused per directory, collides across sibling dirs under a shared home). value+0x08 = home-dir backref OID (the directory the file was first created in, #327). No explicit on-disk HardLinkCount; link count = number of names resolving to the SAME content-bearing type-0x40 record (owner-dir OID, file_id) -- local (parent,file_id) if alloc>0 else home backref to (home,file_id) through any alloc=0 stub; the (home,ordinal,size,created,modified) tuple over-merges AND over-splits and is NOT used (content-aware re-fix 2026-06-19, MD_DATA_RA_006/master J). $SI+0x70 'HardLinkCount' is a embedded-layout field, always 1. description: Primary and backup boot sectors can DIVERGE in the version field, and the driver cannot detect it. ReFS reads sector 0 (primary) then the last LBA (backup) at mount (RefsReadBootSector win11 @135981 / ReadBootSectorForMount insider @231636; backup LBA = totalSectors−1 = `*(VCB+0x1f0)−1`). Validation `RefsIsBootSectorOurs` (win11 @483985) is self-contained — signature + the ROR1+ADD u16 self-checksum at 0x16 (exactly `forefst._vbr_checksum`, now confirmed against the driver) + geometry sanity (0x18/0x20/0x24). There is NO cross-copy CRC64 and NO virtual clock, so the two copies' relative currency is undecidable; the backup is consulted only when the primary read physically FAILS (the fallback loop breaks on read success regardless of validity). Forensic consequences (RD): (a) on a genuine upgrade the backup retains the ORIGINAL pre-upgrade version — confirmed on TWO independent real upgrades: win10to11refs4g_afterwin11mount (primary v3.14 / backup v3.4) and win1122h2test_afteropenedwithinsider (v3.14 / v3.9); only bytes 0x29 (minor) + 0x17 (checksum) differ. This recovers the EXACT original version (vs $VolInfo's "pre-v3.10"). (b) The same divergence reveals VBR tampering: on hand-edited test images the primary carries the altered version (6.66, 3.15) while the backup holds the authentic 3.14. Static caveat (mechanism undetermined): the in-driver RW-mount upgrade dual-writes both copies (RefsWriteBootSector @135517, gated only by the SMR flag CmsVol+0xd34&0x800000), so both *should* be rewritten — yet the backup keeps the old version on every observed upgrade. The offline-tool hypothesis is ruled out: refsutil has no version-upgrade command (applets are dedup/snapshot/salvage/rollback/compression/triage/fixleaks/fixboot/iometrics), and its sole VBR writer `CFixBoot::Execute` (@140032770) also dual-writes primary + backup (decompiled). So the divergence seems to originate inside the driver's own upgrade path — the backup write apparently skipped on the upgrade transaction, or the version stamped via a sector-0-only path — but the exact reason is not pinned down. The empirical signal (backup retains the original version on 2 independent upgrades) is solid; the mechanism is not. Surfaced by `integrity` (Redundancy section reports the version mismatch + both versions, honestly "upgrade or tampering").

description: Deleted directory entries are recoverable in B+-tree NODE SLACK — and no current tool method gets them. Both tools' B+-tree iterators drive strictly off the live row-offset array `[thoff+astart, thoff+aend)`; the ~13 KB of slack in a 16 KB page is never read. Deletion (`CmsBPlusTable::DeleteFromIndex` @14001a610) removes only the offset-array slot and queues *delayed* compaction — row bytes are not scrubbed; they persist until a later CoW rewrite. RD (verified by hand): a slack scan of directory pages on win11refs2tmillionsofactions recovered 179 stale type-0x30 rows whose names are not in the live tree (real deleted names: xbpt_backup_report_125235.md, elvis_dir_zulu_272755, FVE2.{…}). `deleted --scan-pages` visits the right pages but still only follows their live offset array, so it misses these. BUILT as `deleted --slack` (v3.3.3, deletion-recovery "Method 5"): brute-walks free-region row headers, decodes name+MACB+attrs, confidence-graded (high/medium/partial by timestamp sanity), cross-flags deleted vs prior-version. Validated 0 false positives on the clean baseline (all 19 recovered names genuinely absent from the live tree); robust v3.4/64K/corrupt. (Q8) UPDATED (E64, 2026-08-01): the orphan-page slack path now EXISTS as `deleted --full` (so "no current tool method gets them" no longer holds); the deleted-vs-prior split is IDENTITY-based (name + create_time), not a global name test; identical files deleted from several dirs are recovered once with all locations logged (recover-once/log-all); non-resident backings are joined by (file_id, home-backref)+size and carved (Feature C); a deleted parent dir groups children under $DELETED/DIR_OID_0x<oid>; write recoveries with `export deleted DIR`; the old `--slack` flag is now a silent no-op. description: Per-name MACB divergence across hard-link names — a ReFS-only, journal-independent timestomp cross-check. $SI MACB is stored PER NAME (per hard link), not per inode as on NTFS: each name is an independent type-0x30 non-resident row with its own Created(value+0x10)/Modified(+0x18)/Changed(+0x20)/Accessed(+0x28). A name-scoped SetFileTime rewrites only the opened name AND the shared type-0x40 backing; sibling names keep the true birth, so the LATEST Created among siblings is authentic and a backdated name is the stomp. description: Inline integrity checksum element (extends MD_DATA_RA_007): on a v3.14 4K-cluster CRC32-C stream each checksummed cluster is a run_length==1 extent (flag 0x1c00d0) immediately followed by an 8-byte element [CRC32-C(cluster):le32@+0][reserved:le32@+4]; 32-byte stride. description: The per-directory FileId ordinal (NextFileId, $SI+0x58; = lower 8 bytes of the 128-bit USN File ID) is monotonically allocated and NEVER re-used after a deletion (increment-only): a deleted file's reference (containing-dir OID, FileId) is never re-issued to a later file, so USN correlation on that reference is TEMPORALLY stable (no aliasing of a deleted file to a later one across the journal's history). This TEMPORAL no-reuse is DISTINCT from SPATIAL object identity: the ordinal is per-directory scoped (its value recurs across sibling dirs, so it needs the OID), and for HARD-LINKED files the object is resolved by (owner-dir, file_id) SIZE-MATCH (FN_LINK_002 / #340 / E51), not by the ordinal alone. Extends MD_USN_RA_002; cross-ref MD_SI_RA_008.
static_analysis_notes: Increment-only counter: RefsMoveFile increments the parent's NextFileId and stamps the new child; RefsGetNextFileIdFromObjectTable reads the PERSISTED object-record counter (no free-list); RefsDeleteFileId2 / RefsQueueTriageForDeadFileId only remove the type-0x20 FileId-index entry on delete -- nothing decrements or recycles a freed ordinal. description: Embedded-record file whose $DATA is EXTENT-backed ('inline holder'): a key_flags=0x01 type-0x30 value (long, >84 B) holds the file's record, while the $DATA stream's extent map lives in the embedded type-0x80 holder (descriptor 0x00010028). This is simply what an extent-backed file looks like when its record was never split out - i.e. never moved and never hard-linked. On format <=3.10 it is the form of EVERY embedded row (100%), because main $DATA is never inline there; on 3.14 it is 8.1% of embedded rows. Among extent-backed files on 3.14, 34.6% are embedded (never moved/linked) and 65.4% are split. The embedded value is a multi-level B+-tree, so an outer-level parse finds no $DATA row and reports size 0 despite on-disk data (E73 descends it).
static_analysis_notes: Extent runs are the same 24-byte format the driver CmsStream::LookupAllocation reads (E2, MD_SNAP_RA_003); holder descriptor 0x00010028 and residency-via-disk-alloc are E2/RD (structure_reference C.6). Detection is forefst _multilevel_extent_backed_size / _current_stream_extent_backed (F5): get_resident_file_size looks for the 0x80000001 $DATA row in the embedded B+-tree and finds none at the outer level; size@0x58/alloc@0x60 at fixed header offsets. Leaf extents = the rows in the holder's MSB+ B+-tree node index array (node table header tbl[4]/tbl[8]; inner-node bit tbl[3]&0x100) - the standard node structure walk_bplus/_walk parse (E2). forefst's scan instead drops rows with flags & 0x04 (aggregate/fence entries that sit OUTSIDE the leaf index array; on xbpt_archive_romeo the 0x04 row's vlcn==first-leaf and its run spans the leaves), proven IDENTICAL to the node-index-array decode (RD: 855/855 holders, 0 diff). description: Multi-level embedded attribute tree (E73): when a file's attribute set outgrows one embedded node, the node inside the embedded type-0x30 value becomes an INDEX node - descriptor+0x0C level!=0 AND descriptor+0x0D bit0 set - carrying one row per child with an EMPTY separator key (key_offset 0x10, key_size 0x00) whose value is a 48-byte node reference (4x le64 LCNs; 0 and 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF are sentinels). The file's REAL attributes ($DATA 0x80, ADS/$SNAPSHOT 0xB0, $REPARSE 0xC0, and the type-0x0 key_len 0x50 ADS extent records of E61) live in the CHILD PAGE, not in the value; the outer level holds none of them, so an outer-level-only parse returns an empty list and reports a confident 'none' rather than an error. The child is reached with the ordinary page walk. description: Allocator row format (E74), correcting four points of structure_reference B.2. (1) The bitmap row is VARIABLE length: bitmap_offset + roundup8(ceil(range_length/8)); 2072 B is only the range_length=16384 case (also 152 for 1024 clusters, 32 for 12 and 3). (2) +0x14 is TWO u8 fields, not a u16 'header size': bitmap_offset u8@0x14 (0x18 with a bitmap, 0x00 without) and a format byte u8@0x15 that is TIER-dependent - Container and Small are 1 on every version, Medium is 1 on v3.4 and 2 on v3.7+. (3) Flags BIT 0 means 'this row carries a bitmap' - the discriminator the driver uses; values 0x01/0x05/0x09 (bitmap) and 0x02/0x06 (compact) are consequences. (4) +0x16 is NOT a usable used-count: it is a driver-maintained allocated hint with 0xFFFF meaning 'the entire range', it disagrees with the row's own bitmap on 742 of 4634 rows, and must never be used for capacity arithmetic. +0x10 (free) IS authoritative but SATURATES at 0xFFFF (it does not truncate) - impossible on a bitmap row (range <= 16384), so it affects compact rows only. ROW ADDRESSES ARE PHYSICAL cluster numbers for the Medium tier (NOT stated by B.2, and a different question from B.2's Addressing column which describes how each tier's TABLE PAGES are reached): the Medium span is exactly [0, last-mapped-physical-cluster) on every image while the virtual space starts at first_container_id<<shift and is ~2x wider; live file-data extents are marked allocated 99-100% by translated PLCN vs 0-27% by VLCN. Container/Small row address basis NOT established. Authoritative free count: bitmap row = range_length - popcount(bitmap); compact row = 0 if free_u16==0 else range_length. Compact-row discriminator is free_u16 (0 = fully allocated, non-zero = fully free, and then free_u16 == min(range_length,0xFFFF)); this REFUTES the earlier working guess that the discriminator was +0x16.
static_analysis_notes: E2, two independent driver generations. v3.14 CmsAllocator::BPlusRowToRegionEx (win11 @140092a60): start/length u64@0x00/0x08; (u32)u16@0x10 as free with NO sentinel handling; u16@0x12 flags; u16@0x16 into region+0x18 EXPANDING 0xFFFF to range_length; bitmap pointer = value + (u8)value[0x14] ONLY when flags & 1; tests (u8)value[0x15] > 1. Write side CmsAllocator::PersistRegion: value+0x16 = 0xFFFF iff region+0x18 == range_length, else the low 16 bits. v3.4 CmsGlobalAllocator::CopyBPlusRowToFv (win10 @1c0054f50) independently confirms all three: flags&1 gates the bitmap, (u8)value[0x14] is the bitmap offset, and the copy length is range_length>>3 - the variable bitmap size.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-01, all 95 ReFS images of the 99-image corpus, 7063 rows (5695 on pages claiming the tier's own table id). Row size matches the driver's formula on 4634/4634 bitmap rows. bitmap_offset is 24 exactly when flags&1 and 0 otherwise: 5695/5695. free == range_length - popcount on 4634/4634. Compact discriminator resolves 1061/1061 with 0 unexplained. Saturation proven not truncation: a 262144-cluster range (low 16 bits = 0) stores free=0xFFFF. Adversarial: every live metadata cluster on every image is marked ALLOCATED - 0 live-but-free across 95 images (those are PHYSICAL clusters, which is what first indicated the physical row addressing); live FILE DATA is 100% allocated on every healthy image tested (winsider 131385/131385). Address-space proof 2026-09-01: structural (Medium span == physical container extent on 4/4 images, virtual range differs) + behavioural (13917 live extents over 28 images: 99-100% allocated by PLCN per healthy image, 0-27% by VLCN). description: Persisted allocator summary and tier resolution (E74). NEW STRUCTURE: each allocator table's ROOT PAGE carries a 384-byte summary ReFS maintains itself, at _SmsIndexRoot + u16@(_SmsIndexRoot+0x04) = page+0x50+u16@(page+0x54), observed at page+0x78 on every image. Read as u64[48]: slot 1 = clusters covered, slot 2 = free clusters, slot 0 = format (2 on v3.7+ Medium, 1 on v3.4 Medium, 0 on Container/Small); slots 3-8 undecoded. It is the volume's OWN accounting and an independent check on any recomputation. TIER RESOLUTION: on v3.4 the tiers PARTITION (Medium intersect Container = 0 on all 9 v3.4 volumes; the live clusters Medium does not span are covered by Container) and are unioned; on v3.7+ Medium CONTAINS Container (intersection = the entire Container span on 86/86 volumes) so the tiers must NEVER be summed - Medium alone is the authority. COVERAGE LIMIT: the allocator covers only what the Container Table maps; the physical tail [last mapped cluster .. volume end) belongs to no tier - exactly 48 MiB on 90/95 images across every version and both cluster sizes (12288 x 4 KiB = 768 x 64 KiB), being the partial trailing container ReFS never creates; a real volume can leave far more (winsider 924 of a possible 956 containers, 2087 MiB). Report it as outside the allocator, never as free. TIER SELECTION: by table id AND per-page, not by root index (same defect class as #337) - on the four win11refs2tmillionsofactions* volumes root 12 carries table 0x0B not 0x22 and roots 4/6 are empty, and even an ID-correct root is insufficient because root 1's subtree there descends into pages of tables 0x05 and 0x20; accept a row only if its page claims the tier's own table id at page+0x48.
static_analysis_notes: E2: CmsAllocator::LoadAllocatorSummary (win11 @14003ef8c) copies 3 x 0x80 = 384 bytes from _SmsIndexRoot + u16@+0x04 into the allocator object; CommitAllocatorSummary is the write side, and RebuildAllocatorSummary / MarkAllocatorSummaryOutOfSync show the driver itself treats the summary as capable of going stale.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-01, 95 images / 281 tier-instances: the persisted summary agrees with the totals recomputed from the rows on 268, and ALL 13 disagreements are explained - 9 are v3.4 Medium (the summary spans the whole mapped volume while the Medium rows do not, under strict tier separation; the FREE counts still match exactly) and 4 are the damaged millionsofactions family (truncated container table: 16192 of 32767 containers). A disagreement is therefore itself a finding, not a parse failure. 1368 of 7063 rows reached from the tier roots sat on a foreign page - all on those same 4 volumes; on the 91 undamaged images the page-id check rejects nothing. Probe: analysis/tools/analysis_scripts/allocator_summary_check.py.

description: ReFS 3.4 ADS are stored with a MARKER-LESS embedded 0xB0 key (E75): the attribute type sits at key+0x08 and the UTF-16 stream name starts at key+0x0C, whereas from v3.7 an instance marker (0x80000002/0x80000001) occupies key+0x08, the type moves to key+0x0C and the name to key+0x10 - the two-form rule E72/MD_LK_RA_006 already recorded for embedded keys in general. A 0xB0 reader that matches only the marker form therefore reports ZERO alternate data streams on every v3.4 volume. Both forms must be accepted and the name read at the offset the matched form implies. The ADS-vs-snapshot discriminator is unchanged (StreamSummary val+0x10: 0=ADS, 2=snapshot, E61). Marker-less 0xB0 rows also survive on volumes UPGRADED from v3.4 (retained pre-marker entries), so the rule is not purely version-gated and must be applied per-record. These rows are typically NOT at the outer level of the embedded tree - they are reached only via the E73 index-node descent, which is why an outer-level census reported none.
static_analysis_notes: Key layout is the E72/MD_LK_RA_006 two-form rule (marker era boundary v3.4<->v3.7, corroborated by unsound/refsprogs' explicit version>=3.5 branch). The 0xB0 attribute type and the StreamSummary ADS/snapshot discriminator at val+0x10 are the documented E61/C11 fields.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-01. win10refs2tspecials (v3.4, 2 TB): 176 live embedded 0xB0 rows, 0 with a marker, type 0xB0 at key+0x08, all val+0x10==0 (ADS). Reader reported 'ads (0)'; after accepting both key forms it reports 100 ADS-bearing files. Names match the generator exactly (Generate-FSActivity.ps1:1024 $stream='hidden_{0}' -f Rng.Next(1000,9999)) and CONTENT IS BYTE-EXACT vs the generator's two literals: test/xbpt_tango_archive_828215.dat:hidden_1514 -> 'Replayed ADS at 2026-05-16T11:51:08.7086168Z' (:733) and xbpt_data_quebec_921347.tmp:hidden_2136 -> 'Generated ADS at 2026-05-16T11:55:12.4451440Z' (:1024). Corpus census of marker-less embedded 0xB0 rows: 184 over five v3.4 volumes + 4 over two UPGRADED v3.14 volumes. Corpus effect: 7 images change, ALL 0->N (v3.4 win10refs110g 0->2, win10refs5g64k 0->2, win10refs2tspecials 0->100, win10refs8gsetintegristystreams1 0->2, win10to11refs4g_beforewin11mount 0->2; upgraded v3.14 win10to11refs4g 0->2, win10to11refs4g_afterwin11mount 0->2) - strictly additive, 0 lost. Refutes the 2026-08-29 differential audit's finding-#1 verdict ('0 ADS on 3.4 is the correct answer'), whose sweep predated the E73 child-page descent and so could not see these rows.

description: Authoritative file size for a non-resident object (E76). A type-0x30 index-entry name (key_flags 0x02) caches the file size at value+0x38; the OBJECT's size is the type-0x40 backing's value+0x58. The cache is not refreshed on every update and can be stale in BOTH directions - larger than the object (an over-read that appends cluster slack) or SMALLER (a silent truncation, the dangerous case). Any size that gates a read or a write must resolve through the backing when one exists and fall back to the name's field only when it does not. Structurally impossible on v3.4, which has no type-0x40 rows and no key_flags 0x02 FILE rows (only kf=2 directories), so the rule keys on 'a backing resolves' rather than on the volume version.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation. The rule rests on the on-disk corroboration below: the backing's +0x58 agrees with the independently-decoded $DATA stream size where the name's cache does not. The type-0x40 backing layout itself is the documented C.3a structure.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole 99-image corpus: 83,176 key_flags 0x02 FILE rows, all with a resolvable backing; 190 STALE (v3.7:3, v3.9:4, v3.10:18, v3.14:165). In 190/190 the backing +0x58 equals the $DATA-derived stream size and the name +0x38 does not. Divergence runs BOTH ways: hardlink_audit_219848.cfg caches 239973 for a 97673-byte object; hardlink_mike_576693.csv caches 293302 for a 479429-byte object. Extracting the three largest under-read cases recovered 186127/274284/49480 bytes the previous code discarded, each 99.6% non-zero. v3.4 control: 0 type-0x40 rows and 0 kf=2 file rows on win10refs2tspecials/win10refs110g/win10refs5g64k. Fix validated corpus-wide: files --csv byte-identical 99/99; across the 39 affected images all 294 changed dataruns lines are size= lines with 0 extent/cluster changes; golden 90 rows all explained (51 warning-only, 39 size+warning, 0 unexplained).

description: Every MLog LogCore record carries its own 8-byte integrity value at entry_header+0x08 (= page+0x80 where the entry header offset at page+0x54 is 0x78), and the algorithm is REPRODUCIBLE (E78). It is a four-way interleaved u64 XOR folded to 32 bits, not a CRC: zero the 8-byte field itself, then for each log block of le32(page,0x0C) bytes (0x1000 on every volume, independent of the cluster size) accumulate acc[i mod 4] ^= each little-endian u64, XOR the four accumulators together, and fold the result 64->32 as (v>>32) ^ (v & 0xFFFFFFFF). Blocks chain: the next block's acc[0] is seeded with rotate-left-1 of the previous block's result. A record is exactly one block, so in practice the seed is 0. The field is present on BOTH record types at entry_header+0x30: type 1 (control page) and type 2 (data record); no other type exists on disk. The per-volume constant at page+0x04 is a format/log-instance magic, NOT a checksum - reading it as a per-record checksum finds the same value on every record. Because it is an XOR fold it is an integrity check, not a signature: it detects any altered byte but is blind to a REORDERING of 8-byte words that keeps each word in its own lane (i mod 4).
static_analysis_notes: Written by LogCoreWriteDataRecord and verified by LogVerifyChecksumEntryHeader -> LogChecksumBlock on recovery; the log block size is hard-set to 0x1000 by MlLogOpenLog (record+0x0C).
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole 99-image corpus: 599,039 of 599,039 data records recompute EXACTLY, plus 95 of 95 control pages - ReFS 3.4 through 3.15 and Insider, 4K and 64K clusters, 0 mismatches. Every MLog-signature page in every data area is type 2 (599,039 of 599,039); control pages are type 1. Adversarial: 2,000/2,000 random single-bit flips detected; a 0x01 flip at EVERY ONE of the 4,096 byte offsets is detected (0 blind offsets); corrupting the stored field itself is detected; 500 records carry 500 distinct values, so the check is not vacuous. End-to-end on a tampered copy, forefst mlog --stats reports the 2 flipped data records and the flipped control copy and leaves the intact copy verified. Shipped as forefst.mlog_verify_record().

description: The $UsnJrnl:$J journal is an IN-PLACE RING, not an NTFS-style front-trimmed sparse file (E79). A record whose USN is X sits at byte offset X modulo the stream's ALLOCATION, the extents start at file VCN 0, and old records are overwritten where they lie. Consequence for a reader: the whole allocation must be read and the buffer may hold TWO generations at once - the newest records are at the START of the buffer and the oldest in the middle, so byte order is not time order and the highest USN legitimately exceeds the stream's size. Under the alternative (front-trimming) the live extents would begin past VCN 0 and offsets would be USN minus a base; that is refuted below.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the on-disk observation below is decisive on its own because it is a controlled discriminator between the two candidate models.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02. 14 corpus journals, 338,439 of 338,439 records satisfy USN mod allocation == byte offset. The decisive case is winsider.raw, the only journal that has WRAPPED: allocation 33,554,432 B (32 MiB, extents (VCN 0, 6021 cl) + (VCN 6021, 2171 cl) = 8,192 clusters exactly), highest USN 74,459,840 = 2.22 windows, and ALL 217,892 records have USN >= the allocation, so the modulo is never the trivial identity. The buffer holds exactly two generations: generation 1 occupies offsets 7,352,320..33,554,168 and generation 2 occupies 0..7,350,976 - a clean partition with the write head at ~7.35 MB, which is the signature of a ring that has wrapped once. 0 violations. Non-circular: parse_usn_records derives `offset` from the linear scan position and reads `usn` from the record body, so the two quantities are independent. This settles the experiment the reference itself specified for the question.

description: The size of a type-0x30 index-entry value (key_flags 0x02) is fixed AT WRITE TIME by the driver version that created the entry - 72 bytes (0x48) below v3.10, 84 bytes (0x54) from v3.10 - and is NEVER rewritten afterwards (E80). It is therefore NOT a property of the volume: a volume UPGRADED across that boundary carries BOTH layouts side by side, its pre-upgrade entries keeping the 72-byte form while the newer driver writes 84-byte entries for anything new. A reader must take the entry size from the row's own length, never from the volume version; keying on the version misparses every retained entry on an upgraded volume. All fields the tools read live at or below value+0x44, which is identical in both layouts, so a length RANGE test (0x48 <= len <= 84) is correct and version-independent.
static_analysis_notes: The write-time gate is explicit in RefsAddFileNameIndexEntry: the value length is 0x48 when the version is below 0x309 and 0x54 otherwise. The driver applies it when ADDING an entry, which is why existing entries survive an upgrade unchanged.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole 99-image corpus: 2,172 x 72-byte and 113,356 x 84-byte index-entry values. Exactly 3 images carry BOTH, and all 3 are the corpus's UPGRADED volumes (forefst summary: APPEARS UPGRADED): win10to11refs4g and win10to11refs4g_afterwin11mount (32 x 72 B + 6 x 84 B) and win1122h2test_afteropenedwithinsider (482 x 72 B + 333 x 84 B). Every NATIVE volume carries one size only, matching its format-time version. Two controlled BEFORE/AFTER pairs prove the retention on two independent upgrade paths: win10to11refs4g_beforewin11mount (v3.4, 33 x 72 B, 0 x 84 B) -> win10to11refs4g (v3.14, 32 x 72 B + 6 x 84 B), and win1122h2test (v3.9, 482 x 72 B, 0 x 84 B) -> win1122h2test_afteropenedwithinsider (v3.14, the SAME 482 x 72 B retained + 333 x 84 B new). No tool change: forefst already tests the length range rather than the version.

description: The REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER of a DIRECTORY reparse point (junction or directory symlink) is NOT a top-level type-0xC0 row in the object's table: it lives INSIDE the object record's embedded attribute tree (E81). The object's table holds a single row keyed 0x10 whose value carries the embedded tree - typically 0xC0 (reparse), 0x90 and 0x39 - and the parent's name row is an 84-byte index entry with no room for a buffer. The embedded 0xC0 value has a 12-byte header whose u32 at +0x08 is the offset of the standard REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER (tag u32@0x00, ReparseDataLength u16@0x04, Reserved u16@0x06, then SubstituteNameOffset/Length and PrintNameOffset/Length u16 pairs; path buffer at +0x14 for SYMLINK, which carries a 4-byte Flags field, and +0x10 for MOUNT_POINT). A reader that scans only top-level rows reports these targets as absent although they are fully present on disk. A junction commonly carries PrintNameLength 0, so the SubstituteName is the authoritative fallback and the target must never degrade to the tag NAME. Same wrong-level class as E73 (attributes in a child node), so the embedded parse must be given the descent context or an object with a large attribute set is missed a second way.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation. The buffer itself is the documented Windows REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER; what is established here is WHERE ReFS stores it for a directory reparse point, which the on-disk evidence below settles.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole 99-image corpus: of 341 reparse-bearing objects, 243 carry 0xC0 at the top level and 98 carry it ONLY embedded - including 78 of 81 on the real Windows volume winsider.raw. Decoding the embedded buffers yields real targets (\??\C:\ProgramData, \??\C:\Users\Default, Program Files, Common Files, Internet Explorer, Windows Defender, Microsoft Shared - the Windows compatibility junctions). NON-CIRCULAR ground truth: the lab generator writes its own CSV log onto the volume; extracting forefst_test2_log_20260705_085450.csv from win11refs8g gives the 8 reparse points it created with their intended targets. Before the fix the tool found all 8 and resolved the 6 FILE symlink targets byte-for-byte but reported NO target for the 2 DIRECTORY ones (junction1, sym_dir_abs); after it, both resolve to the generator's recorded R:\forefst_test2\reparse\rp_target_dir (the junction via its NT-namespace SubstituteName \??\R:\...). Corpus effect of the fix: 98 targets GAINED over 11 images, 0 changed, 0 lost - strictly additive.

description: Record PLACEMENT and data RESIDENCY are independent axes (E82). A key_flags 0x02 name means the object's record was split out into a type-0x40 backing - what a move or a hard link forces - and says NOTHING about where the file's bytes live. The bytes can remain INSIDE that backing: its MAIN $DATA sub-record (single-instance marker 0x80000001 + type 0x80) is then the RESIDENT form - summary_size@0x0C=0x30, storage_type@0x10=0, byte count at +0x20, content at +0x3C. The alternative is the extent-bearing stream record (inner_hdr@0x00=0x88, summary_size 0x200 on v3.14+ / 0x1A0 on v3.4-v3.10, extents at +0x88); the two forms are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. Two reader traps: an ADS is a MULTI-instance (0x80000002) 0x80 row, so matching any 0x80 row returns a stream that is not the file's data; and the backing must be joined on the PAIR (stream_idx = name value+0x00, home = name value+0x08) -> backing key (+0x08, +0x10), because stream indices are unique per home, not globally. Consequence: a reader that infers residency from key_flags reports these files non-resident and cannot recover their content, though it is in the record already held.
static_analysis_notes: The driver's read path validates the attribute with RefsCheckValidResidentDataAttribute and reads the bytes IN PLACE at content offset 0x38 from the attribute header (= value+0x3C); it never consults a name-row placement flag, so residency is a property of the ATTRIBUTE. RefsAllocateNonResidentDataAttribute is the separate path that moves a stream out.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole 99-image corpus: 16,191 of 83,176 key_flags 0x02 files keep their data inline in the backing, over 26 images (winsider 14,580 of 72,709); mutually exclusive with the extent-bearing form (0 records carry both). Content validated on 400+ sampled files: 400/400 inline length == stated size == the name's cached size; 56/57 .xml parse as well-formed XML; 13/13 .png carry the PNG magic; 5/5 .json parse. NON-CIRCULAR ground truth: the lab generator wrote hl1_/hl2_/hl3_ hard links as exactly 400 bytes of a repeated marker (New-Marked "HL1BODY_" 400, corroborated by its own on-volume STATE log size=400) and the recovered bytes are BYTE-EXACT 7/7. Extends C.3a, which already recorded the phenomenon at backing+0x60 (alloc == size for small files stored resident inside the backing, 6,794/6,823 sub-cluster backings on winsider) but gave no decode for the content. Tool effect: extract/dataruns/export previously failed 'no extents decoded' on these and now read them (25/25 sampled across 3 images, 0 content mismatches); IsResident corrected on 14,118 cells over 14 images, with no other CSV column and no row count changed.

description: Stream snapshots are copy-on-write, so a snapshotted file's data is SHARED across its streams (E83). A block is duplicated only when it is about to be OVERWRITTEN; every block unmodified since a snapshot stays shared - present once on disk, listed in the snapshot's extent table and ABSENT from the current stream's. Consequence for the $DATA stream record: disk_alloc@0x48 is what THIS stream owns (what its own extent list covers) while total_alloc@0x30 is the FILE's whole allocation, so they diverge exactly by the shared (or sparse) blocks. Reading any version means resolving each file VCN across the streams: for the CURRENT stream a missing VCN comes from the NEWEST snapshot holding it (a block only leaves the current table while unchanged); for a PRIOR version only snapshots STRICTLY OLDER may be used, since a newer snapshot can hold content written after the version being recovered. A VCN no stream holds is a genuine sparse hole. A reader that assembles a stream from its own extents alone returns the full size with the shared blocks ZERO-FILLED - bytes present nowhere on the volume.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the on-disk evidence is decisive on its own because the stream record's own extent-count field confirms the short extent list, and the reconstruction is validated byte-exact against independently recorded generator content.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02. Worked case win11refs8g snapfile_03.txt: current stream 0x1000 stream_size=22688, total_alloc=24576 (6 clusters), disk_alloc=8192, extent-count field=2 covering file VCNs 4-5 ONLY; VCNs 0-2 are in snapshot 0x1001 and VCN 3 in 0x1002. Allocation-field semantics measured over 38,378 stream records: no snapshots -> total==disk on 38,286 and total>disk on 38 (sparse); snapshots present -> total>disk on 39 of 54. Defect scope: 8 distinct files (32 rows over 4 images of one lab family), 655,360 bytes silently zero-filled by extract; 0 on the real Windows volume winsider (needs refsutil streamsnapshot THEN a modification). Where the current stream owns NO clusters (snapshotted, never modified) the pre-existing CoW fallback was already correct - a 13.4 MB file extracts fully - so a first structural count of 39 files/14.1 MB overstated it. GROUND TRUTH (non-circular): the generator wrote snapfile_NN as 4096*N bytes of a marker then snapshotted and appended in a recorded sequence; after the fix 8/8 current files and 20/20 prior versions are BYTE-EXACT against that specification (versions were 8/20 before). Sparse files byte-identical, holes still zero.

description: The SECOND u16 of a page-level row-index slot is a MARKER, not a counter (E84 - refutes the refsprogs-sourced GN_TREE_RP_002 'cumulative cluster count saturating at 0xFFFF'). Corpus-wide it takes exactly two values, 0xFFFF and 0, and nothing else. 0 appears ONLY on inner nodes, exactly once per page, always on the LAST slot, and always on a row with an EMPTY key (key_offset 0x10, key_size 0) whose value is a 48- or 72-byte page reference - the B+-tree's RIGHTMOST CHILD pointer (the child covering keys above every separator key). tag==0 implies an empty key with no exception; the converse does NOT hold (269 keyless rows carry 0xFFFF). The marker is written from v3.10 onward; on v3.4-v3.9 the same keyless slot carries 0xFFFF. Leaf slots never carry it. A reader must not treat the field as data: the embedded-tree parser's use of 0xFFFF as its slot-validity terminator is consistent with this, and the page-level walker correctly ignores it.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the on-disk census is decisive because the field is exhaustively two-valued over 843,408 slots and its single non-default value coincides exactly with the keyless rightmost-child row.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole corpus: 843,408 slots -> 0xFFFF 842,529, 0 879, no other value. All 879 zeros are on inner pages, one per page, always the last slot, always a row with key_offset 0x10 / key_size 0 and a 48-byte (858) or 72-byte (21) value. tag==0 -> empty key 879/879, 0 counterexamples; converse fails on 269 keyless rows tagged 0xFFFF. Version split: v3.10/3.14/3.15/6.66 write the 0 marker (879 pages); v3.4/3.7/3.9 never do (216 pages keyless-with-0xFFFF, 0 exceptions). Of the 53 v3.14 keyless-0xFFFF pages, 48 are the three UPGRADED volumes retaining pre-upgrade pages (same write-time retention as E80) and 5 are one Container-Table (table 0x0B) inner page of 189 slots, one on each 2 TB volume. 15,642 leaf pages: 0 markers.

description: A non-inline stream's EXTENT record (the type-0x0 sub-record of E61) is identified by its key SHAPE: key_offset 0x10, key_size 0x50, and attribute type 0x0003 at key+0x08 (E84 - confirms the refsprogs-sourced MD_ADS_RP_001 and sharpens it). Every such record carries a plausible stream size at value+0x38, which is the link back to the 0xB0 stream descriptor. The key itself carries NO stream name - the name is in the 0xB0 descriptor - so 'named-stream extent key' describes the record's purpose, not its key content. A reader must NOT identify the record by a zero byte at key[12]: a DIFFERENT record (14-byte key, attribute type 0x0080 at key+0x08) also satisfies that, and value+0x38 is not a stream size there.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the discriminator is established by the exhaustive on-disk split below (key shape vs plausibility of the stream-size field), which separates the two record types with no overlap.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02, whole corpus. key_offset==0x10 holds on 2,908/2,908 records the shipped reader resolves and 2,994/2,994 in a wider structural population. Key sizes split exactly two ways: 0x50 with type 0x0003 at key+0x08 (657 records, value+0x38 a plausible size on 657/657) and 0x0E with type 0x0080 (2,350 records, value+0x38 implausible - larger than the volume - on 2,330). Neither key form contains a decodable UTF-16 name. Tool: _stream_extent_records filtered on len(k)>12 and k[12]==0x00, which for a 14-byte key tests padding and admitted 2,382 wrong-type rows; measured impact 0 (no loose row shares a real record's stream size on any corpus image, so no ADS was ever mis-resolved). Tightened to the exact test; ads --json, files --csv and specials --json byte-identical on 297/297 corpus runs.

description: An extent entry's cluster number in an inline 0x10028 holder is a VIRTUAL LCN and must be validated by TRANSLATION, never by comparison against the volume's physical cluster count (E85). The virtual address space is wider than the physical one - it begins at (first_container_id << shift) and runs roughly twice as far (E74) - so a plausibility test of the form 0 < vlcn < physical_cluster_count rejects every extent that lives in the upper half of the virtual space. Because a greedy decoder stops at the first entry it cannot validate, one rejected entry makes the whole extent map decode as EMPTY and the file appears to have an undecodable/overflow holder. The correct test is whether the container table can map the VLCN; a physical bound is only a fallback where no translator is available. A sparse entry (vlcn == 0) remains valid and is zero-filled, never read.
static_analysis_notes: Not isolated to a decompiled citation; the on-disk proof is decisive - the rejected VLCN translates cleanly through the documented container table and the clusters it names reproduce the volume's own recorded SHA-256.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-02 on win11bidule.raw (v3.14, 4 GB, 4K clusters), which ships its own SHA-256 inventory of 629 files written by the volume's operator. Worked case logs/allfiles.csv (60,490 B): holder carries 2 extents - vlcn 0x17a799 fvcn 0 run 1, vlcn 0x17a79a fvcn 1 run 14 - a contiguous 15-cluster cover equal to disk_alloc 61,440. vlcn 1,550,233 exceeds the physical count 1,044,480 and was rejected, yet translates to PLCN 731,033; reading those clusters by hand reproduces the recorded SHA-256 exactly. Effect of the correction on that volume: files matching their recorded hash go from 41 to 608 of 629 (the remaining 21 are 1 MB-791 MB files hitting the documented multi-page overflow-holder residual, all failing cleanly). No regression: extract on all 95 golden targets of the existing corpus is byte-identical and every dataruns summary is unchanged, because the correction touches content recovery rather than residency classification. Unseen until now because no image in the 99-image corpus places live file extents above the physical cluster count in virtual space.

description: A file's extent map is a B+-tree NODE inside its $DATA record, not a flat run array (E86). The current stream's $DATA value carries at value+0x88 a node with the standard 0x28-byte header: level at +0x0C (0 = leaf, non-zero = index), row count at +0x14, node size at +0x20, and a trailing index array of 4-byte slots (u16 row offset, u16 key hint = the row's file VCN truncated). LEAF rows are the standard 24-byte C.4 extent entries (VLCN +0x00, file VCN +0x0C, run +0x14). INDEX rows carry the standard 48-byte four-LCN node reference; those LCNs are VIRTUAL and the child page holds the same node at 0x50 + u32@page+0x50, so the walk is uniform and recursive. NEW FIELD: record_size at +0x0A is 24 for a plain run and 24 + run*4 when the stream carries per-cluster CRC32-C (flag bit 0x80 at +0x08), the trailing u32s being those checksums, 4 bytes each. The field takes 136 distinct values (24..1048) and for checksummed records tracks the run across the full observed range (run 11->68, 66->288, 100->424, 122->512, 223->916), which a high-half-of-flags reading cannot produce. Records are 8-BYTE ALIGNED: the step to the next record is roundup8(record_size), measured on 30,524 consecutive row pairs (30,405 match; 428 genuinely padded; 119 larger gaps = unused node space, harmless because rows are addressed by the index array). This also explains WHICH files failed before: the old walk advanced '32 if u32@+0x08 == 0x1c00d0 else 24', and 0x1c00d0 is only the run==1 case, so a checksummed record with run>1 (u32 0x020000d0 at run 122) made it advance 24 and land mid-record - 19 of the 21 unreadable files on the reference volume were integrity streams. This CORRECTS C.4/C.4a: entry+0x08 is u16 flags + u16 row_size, not a u32 flags field - reading the pair as one u32 gives (row_size<<16)|flags, which is why every documented flag constant begins 0x18 (= 24, the plain row size). The $DATA row MUST be selected on the sub-stream id at key+0x10 == 0x1000: a file with snapshots carries one $DATA row per version (0x1001, 0x1002, ...) under the same key prefix, so choosing by value size or first match returns a SNAPSHOT's extents and presents that older version's bytes as the live file. Resolves the residual recorded in C.3b.
static_analysis_notes: Decoded from the on-disk bytes; the node header, level byte and 48-byte four-LCN child reference are the same shapes the driver's own B+-tree walk uses elsewhere (already E2-confirmed for page-level nodes).
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-03. Row-size rule measured over 48,474 extent rows across 40 images: 0 violations of row_size == 24 + (flags&0x80 ? run*4 : 0); observed flag lows 0x40/0x50/0x60 (plain, row_size 24, 47,728 rows) and 0xD0 (checksummed, 746 rows). NON-CIRCULAR ground truth: win11bidule ships the operator's own SHA-256 inventory written on Windows before the image reached this project - files matching it go from 608 to 629 of 629, 0 mismatch. The 21 gained were all >1 MB (19 integrity-stream drivers, a 782 MB archive, a 791 MB ISO) and each had previously failed CLEANLY with 0 bytes; verified end-to-end through extract, including the 791 MB file. Structure present on 54 of 100 corpus images. The sub-stream selector is not cosmetic: selecting the $DATA row by size returned tests/secret.txt's 79-byte pre-truncation snapshot text as the live 25-byte file - caught by hash comparison, not assumption. Implemented as a FALLBACK ONLY (runs where the existing cascade yielded nothing), with _contiguous_cover still applied, so an incomplete walk yields no extents rather than wrong bytes and no previously-resolving file can change. Two decoder defects surfaced while validating this: tr.tr() does NOT raise on a container-table miss - it falls back to IDENTITY (VLCN read as PLCN) and counts the miss, so a direct call would accept an unmappable row and read the WRONG clusters (now tested as (vlcn >> tr.shift) in tr.map, without the counter); and because that counter is surfaced to the analyst as 'N VLCN(s) had no container mapping - output may be incomplete', probing rows that never become extents moved it (541->550 on one image with nothing incomplete). Translation is now deferred until a cover is accepted. With both fixed the whole-corpus output fingerprint (3,496 runs) shows dataruns byte-identical to the previous release on every image. description: Data residency is decided by a VOLUME-FORMAT gate, not by size alone. RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite branches on the volume format version read from the VCB (CONCAT11(vcb[0x318],vcb[0x319]) vs 0x30b=3.11): on format <3.11 a inline write >0x20000 (128 KiB) raises 0xC0000427 STATUS_FILE_SYSTEM_LIMITATION (the v3.4 path calls RefsTelemetryUnsupportedADS, identifying it as the named-stream cap) and an already-inline stream NEVER converts; on format >=3.11 the stream stays inline only while size < 0x800 (2048 B), else RefsConvertToNonResident. Main $DATA is never created resident before format 3.11, so <=3.10 volumes are always extent-backed. Snapshot creation, enabling integrity streams, block-clone, encryption, remote/tiering, strictly-sequential and explicit set-allocation/set-EOF each convert an inline stream to extents regardless of size. The gate reads the VOLUME's format, so an upgrade affects future writes only and converts nothing retroactively.
static_analysis_notes: RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite win11 26100 @1400ddd2c: version gate CONCAT11(vcb[0x318],vcb[0x319]) < 0x30b; error branch 0x20000 -> RefsRaiseStatusInternal(-0x3ffffbd9 = 0xC0000427), WPP trace logs 0xc0000427; residency branch 'format<0x30b || size<0x800' stays resident else RefsConvertToNonResident. win10 17134 @1c00b05a0 has NO conversion branch and calls RefsTelemetryUnsupportedADS on the >0x20000 path; RefsConvertToNonResident is ABSENT from the v3.4 driver (0 refs; 15 each in win11 26100 / 26100.8521 / Insider 29574). RefsCheckValidResidentDataAttribute exists only in the v3.14-era drivers. Complete v3.14 caller set of RefsConvertToNonResident: CreateStreamSnapshot, DuplicateExtents, AddAllocationForResidentWrite, ReplaceDataAttribute, SetEncryption, CascadesSetFileRemote, SetFileStrictlySequential, SetAllocationInfo, SetEndOfFileInfo.

description: READER DEFECT (found 2026-09-04, NOT fixed). A key_flags 0x02 name whose HOME object is never walked as a directory never has its type-0x40 backing registered in walk_directory_tree's t40_content map (keyed (owner_oid, stream_idx) and filled only from visited directories), so resolution falls to the solo branch with rec=None and data_inline is left unset. files then reports IsResident=False although the backing's $DATA is the inline form. Content is NOT affected: extract resolves the backing on demand via _home_streams and returns the right bytes, labelled resident/inline. Fix: give the walk the same cached on-demand obj_map[home] lookup. High blast radius (the same rec feeds hard-link grouping, USN, SecurityId, attrs).

description: Named streams follow the same 0x800 (2048 B) threshold as main $DATA on format >=3.11, one-directionally: NO named stream of 2048 B or more is inline, and extent-backed ones start at exactly 2048. Below 2 KiB a stream is inline UNLESS the writer pre-allocated (alloc != size; E60), which is why 13 sub-2KiB streams are extent-backed. The documented ATTRIBUTE-FLAGS u16 at value+0x02 is the exact discriminator: bit 0x1000 set <=> content is not inline (729 extent-backed + 115 snapshot-name), clear <=> inline or empty (7,509), 0 violations. 0xB0 rows with storage_type 2 are NOT an ADS storage form: they are named SNAPSHOT entries whose value+0x44 matches an existing $DATA sub-id > 0x1000 (115/115). The 0x20000 (128 KiB) cap is an error branch that fires only on format <3.11; on v3.14 a 131,072-byte named stream stores normally.

description: The NAMED_DATA attribute-flags u16 at 0xB0 value+0x02 carries the named-stream residency discriminator. Bit 0x1000 is SET on every stream whose content is not inline (extent-backed streams and snapshot entries) and CLEAR on every inline stream and inline-form empty. This CORRECTS NAMED_DATA.md's parenthetical that 0x1000 'does not mean non-resident - such ADS are still inline': that reading is explained by 13 rows which look inline only if the E60 packed-allocation rule is not applied (an inline named stream stores its bytes packed, alloc == size; all 13 have alloc 4096 with size 7 or 30 and are extent-backed). Other bits observed but NOT interpreted: 0x0C00 accompanies 0x1000 on snapshot entries (giving 0x1C00, consistent with the page's existing HasSnapshot 0x0400 note), and 0x4000 accompanies 0x1000 on the 12 SmartScreen streams (giving 0x5000). Both recorded as observed, meaning not established - they are not named as flags.
static_analysis_notes: No driver citation for this field yet: the residency GATE is decompiled (RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite, MD_DATA_RA_025) but the write of this flag is not traced. SECOND ELEMENT NOT AVAILABLE IN-WORKSPACE: refsprogs source is not present (only the 2026-08-29 audit ledger, which records refsprogs deciding residency 'by attribute form' at L9-I01 but does not quote this field), so the requested independent reading could not be checked. Corroboration used instead: the E60 packed-allocation rule, which is forefst's own validated extraction path, and the internal cross-check that every 0x1C00 row is a snapshot entry independently witnessed by a matching $DATA sub-id > 0x1000 (115/115).

Bit 0x1000 set on exactly 844 rows (729 extent-backed + 115 snapshot entries) and clear on exactly 7,509 (7,505 inline + 4 inline-form empty). ZERO violations of 'bit set <=> content not inline'. Observed values: 0x0000 (7,509), 0x1000 (717), 0x1C00 (115), 0x5000 (12).

This is the driver-side counterpart of the on-disk fact that main $DATA is never inline before format 3.11: the older driver has neither the check for a resident DATA attribute nor any way to convert one out of line.

description: The driver reads the VOLUME FORMAT VERSION from the VCB as two bytes at +0x318 (major) and +0x319 (minor), combined as CONCAT11(vcb[0x318], vcb[0x319]) - i.e. (major << 8) | minor, so format 3.11 is 0x30B. This is the field every format-gated behaviour branches on, and it is the VOLUME's format, not the driver's build: an up-to-date driver mounting an older-format volume takes the older branch. Observed comparison constants in v3.14: 0x30b (3.11) and 0x309 (3.9).
static_analysis_notes: refs.sys win11 26100: RefsAddAllocationForResidentWrite @1400ddd2c reads it twice, via the SCB's VCB pointer at scb+0x90. Six occurrences of the '< 0x30b' comparison and two of '< 0x309' in that build. The values compared are real ReFS FORMAT versions (3.9, 3.11), which a driver-version field would not be.
raw_analysis_notes: Behavioural confirmation on disk, without a VM: on win10to11refs4g (a v3.4 volume upgraded to v3.14) 0 of 262 pre-existing files changed residency, while the only inline file (desktop.ini, 129 B) is one of exactly 3 names that appear only AFTER the upgrade. Residency is therefore fixed at write time by the volume's then-current format, which is what a VCB-inline format field predicts.

description: $EFS DDF entry layout decoded. val[0x60] u32 = DDF entry count (1 on every observed record - single user, no data-recovery agent, so no DRF). The single DDF entry starts at val[0x64] with a 5-u32 header: [0x64] entry_len, [0x68] hash_len = 0x14 (SHA-1), [0x6C] wrapped-FEK length = 0x100 (RSA-2048), [0x70] FEK offset RELATIVE TO 0x64, [0x74] zero. Fixed-offset fields inside the entry: credential SID at val[0x94] (28B, S-1-5-21-...), public-key-info header at val[0xB0] (5 u32s, first = 0x14 hash length), certificate SHA-1 thumbprint at val[0xC4] (20B = 0xB0 + 0x14), container-GUID/CSP/key-container UTF-16LE strings from val[0xD8]. Two invariants hold on every record: 0x64 + entry_len == value_len - 2 and 0x64 + FEK_offset + 0x100 == value_len - 2, so the wrapped FEK is the entry's last field and the value carries 2 trailing bytes. Resolves both value sizes: FEK at val[0x1A2] on 676B records and val[0x1DA] on 732B.
static_analysis_notes: Not traced in the driver: EFS metadata is produced by the EFS service/cng.sys, not by refs.sys (GN_EFS_SA_001 records the driver-side integration only). The layout is the DPAPI/EFS DDF format, decoded here on disk.
raw_analysis_notes: 7/7 $EFS records over 3 images (win11refs4gattributestest2 4, win11refs4gattributes 2, wininsiderrefs2t 1) satisfy all four invariants: DDF count == 1, hash_len 0x14 / FEK 0x100 / pad 0 / pk[0] 0x14, 0x64+entry_len == len-2, 0x64+FEKoff+0x100 == len-2. Both value sizes present (676B x6, 732B x1). Thumbprint at 0xC4 is constant within a certificate set and differs between them, as a per-user cert must. BREADTH CAVEAT: v3.14+ only, DDF count 1 only - no multi-user or DRA-bearing record exists in the corpus, so the count>1 and DRF-present layouts are UNVERIFIED.

description: Per-volume compression parameters live in the CONTAINER TABLE ROOT PAGE header, not in a row: u32 marker at page+0xA0, u16 format at +0xA4, i16 level at +0xA6, u32 chunk size at +0xA8. The marker is VERSION-KEYED, not the constant 0x0F previously recorded (E90): 0x07 on v3.4 format, 0x0F on v3.7+. Format enum 0=None 1=LZ4 2=ZSTD 3=LZ4QAT; only 1 and 2 occur on disk. Claim is scoped to root pages that parse as an index root (descriptor thoff==0x228).
static_analysis_notes: Algorithm set corroborated by GN_COMP_SA_001 (win11 26100 embeds ZSTD + LZ4; win10 17134 has CmsCompressionLZX only).
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-05 over 100 images: 89 carry a container-table root page, 85 parse as an index root. 0xA0 == 0x07 on 13/13 v3.4 pages (12x 4K, 1x 64K); 0x0F on 72/72 v3.7+ pages (3.7x1, 3.9x2, 3.10x2, 3.14x64, 3.15x1, +2 version-edited v3.14). No cross-over. 10 images have 0xA4 != 0: format 1 x7 / 2 x3, levels 1,3,7,9,11,13,15, chunk 0x1000/0x8000/0x20000/0x40000. OUT OF SCOPE: 4 x 2TB millionsofactions images have thoff==0x8 (not an index root) and read 0xA0=0x4004 - a different frame, not a counter-example (E49 trap). UNVERIFIED: format 3 (LZ4QAT) has no on-disk instance; the u32 at +0x98 is 0 on v3.4/v3.7 and 4 on v3.9+ except 2 v3.14 pages that read 0 - left in open_questions.

description: Block-refcount value length is exactly 0x820 (2,080 B): 28-byte header (0x00..0x1B, TotalRefCount at +0x18) + u16[1024] per-cluster array at 0x1C..0x81B + a 4-byte field at 0x81C..0x81F. That trailing field is NOT padding and NOT a zero constant: it is a field of UNKNOWN MEANING that is zero on most rows and carries structured content on the rest.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-05: 1,441 rows over 41 images. Value length == 0x820 on 1,441/1,441; le32@0x18 == sum(entry & 0x3FFF) on 1,441/1,441. The 0x81C field is non-zero on 159/1,441 rows (11.0%), taking 15 distinct values over 8 images (winsider 106, wininsiderrefs2t 23, win1122h2test_afteropenedwithinsider 13, millionsofactionsv2 7, wininsiderrefs8gtest2 4, +3 more). EVERY non-zero instance has high u16 == 0xFFFF; the low u16 varies (0x9000 x74, 0xf805 x25, 0x90b4 x17, 0xbb00 x9, ...). ALL 159 are on v3.14 volumes; 0 on v3.4-v3.10. MECHANISM UNDETERMINED: 0xFFFF is the marker the page row-offset table uses, but the low u16 exceeds a 16 KiB page on these 4 KiB-cluster volumes, so the obvious 'adjacent row-index slot' reading does not hold on magnitude. Recorded as measured, not explained.

description: The page-reference checksum is computed over the WHOLE referenced PAGE - the concatenation of the cluster bytes of every valid LCN slot at page-reference +0x00..+0x18, read AFTER container translation - and is compared against the value at page-reference +0x28 (length from +0x24, algorithm from +0x22). In an Object-Table row the page reference begins at value+0x20, so the LCN slots are value+0x20..0x38 and the checksum is at value+0x48. Slot count is determined by cluster size, not by version: 4 slots on 4 KiB clusters and 1 on 64 KiB, both yielding one page (16 KiB / 64 KiB). Nothing is excluded from the digest - not the page header, not the page's own self-checksum field. Where an Object Table holds several rows for one object id, only the row the reader keeps (the last) is meaningful.
static_analysis_notes: Reproduced from the bytes rather than from the driver; the pre-v3.14 verification behaviour documented on the page (CmsChecksumNone stub) is a separate, decompilation-only claim and is untouched by this row.
raw_analysis_notes: RD 2026-09-05, every Object-Table page reference on 89 images: 34,311 checked, 0 skipped. The invariant is scoped to the row the READER uses: an Object Table may carry MORE THAN ONE row per object id (an earlier generation and a current one) and build_object_map keeps the LAST. On that row the digest verifies 33,883/33,883 - 89/89 images, no carve-out, no tolerance. The remaining 428 references are SUPERSEDED rows; 408 of them still verify and 20 do not, which says nothing about the volume because nothing reads them. Duplicate rows occur on 4 images only (the win11refs2tmillionsofactions family, 107 of 200 oids doubled). By cluster size: 4 slots on every 4 KiB reference, 1 on every 64 KiB one, both making one page. Both algorithms exercised: type 0x02 CRC64 and type 0x04 SHA-256.
